proposedEntry.name: accessible-content
proposedEntry.description: Writes and structures user-facing content -- labels, headings, error messages, alt text, link text, form instructions, data tables -- so it works for screen readers, second-language readers, and people under stress. Targets a 12-14 reading age with one idea per sentence and active voice; enforces a logical, non-skipped heading hierarchy used for structure rather than visual styling; requires visible, programmatically-associated form labels plus required-field indication and error association (aria-describedby); gives a decision table for alt text by image type (informative, decorative, functional, complex, image-of-text); bans context-free link text ('click here', 'read more') in favour of descriptive links; structures error messages as [what happened] + [what to do] without blaming the user; and specifies data-table markup (caption, scoped headers, no layout tables). Ends with an eight-item content-review checklist covering labels, heading hierarchy, link text, error messages, alt text, reading level, and translatability.

#### Owl-Listener/designpowers (inspected 2026-08-29)

See usability-testing.json for shared repo-level evidence (HEAD SHA, stars, license, full 36-skill enumeration). accessible-content: relevance 3 (content that must work for screen readers and plain-language readers is core, specific WCAG-adjacent work), quality 3 (concrete reading-level target, an alt-text decision table by image type, specific ARIA-association rules for labels and errors, and an eight-item review checklist), conformance 2 (single self-contained file, no links, frontmatter is name+description only), uniqueness 2 (registry's ux-writing covers general microcopy/voice/tone but has no dedicated alt-text decision table, heading-hierarchy-for-screen-readers guidance, or aria-describedby error-association rule -- this is a distinct accessibility-of-content lens the content-design category currently lacks). Total 10, vendor.
